Thank you very much for your comment! :D

The oddly paced maybe is because of the separation of days, but I think that's not an excuse, I must pay more attention to that while writing, thank you for pointing it out!

I'm very glad you liked it. I was actually waiting for you to read it for a while, hehe. As the creator of the GoI I was very curious about your opinion on the article, and I'm very happy that it was to your liking.

About the alt. reality, yes

Extract for the canon I'm making with my ES pals:
collapsibles are our friends

Wilson Wildlife Solutions is a paranormal wildlife project funded by the Foundation and based in the United States, Japan, and Latin America. Although initially a state project and known to exist since 1999, it was not until the Megaptera Incident in 2001 that its existence was officially recognized and a relationship established between the two groups. Currently, the Boring Agreement describes that Wilson Wildlife Solutions must be supervised by DMs specializing in wildlife in the Regions in which it operates, and that they can handle anomalies based on wildlife containment that are either Safe or Euclid with varying degrees of Foundation intervention (on a case-by-case basis). Amendments to the Boring Agreement can be, and have been, made to take into account grey areas or new policies as necessary.

In the canon they are much more expanded than usual, and The Foundation has much more confidence in them. They have a very good image in the anomalous world and Tim Wilson is considered by some to be an anomalous 'celebrity'.

Facility-57 canon has its hub translate to english thanks to Tio Nicolini

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
New interpretations of Wilson's Wildlife Solutions, what fun! There are a lot of little lore pieces in here that make me very happy with how people are taking WWS and just running with it — I like the idea that the SCP Foundation is monitorying anomalous communities and acting as a kind of police, but without automatically imprisoning everyone. I like WWS becoming well known enough to be shopping their expertise out to different geographical regions. That's pretty fantastic. I think it totally makes sense that the Amazon would have so much anomalous wildlife, and that Wilson's would consequently become very involved there. I like the idea of a GoI format where it's a public warning about anomalous wildlife — the magical equivalent of mountain lion warnings, saying, "if you see me, don't move", and stuff like that. Basically, lots of little lore things here that I am very much enjoying.

If I were to have a complaint, it would be that the progression of the emails afterwords feels a bit oddly paced? Incinideer are too dangerous to let wander, okay so we'll contain them, wait we can't because natives are keeping the sanctity of their jungle, okay so you'd better come down here and set up shop 'cause this place is more anomalous than North America, alright we will. The progression is not necessarily bad, it just feels… incompletely built? I dunno.

In any case, it's not too large a complaint. I like all the ideas at play here. +1

P.S. This is in an alt. reality where WWS comes under Foundation supervision prior to 2008 (the Ursus Maritimus Incident)?

item.content:encoded:
All hail Incinideer!

I could honestly have gone without the supplemental notes, I think the format standing alone is strong enough but I see the justification of leaving the door open for future Wilson's stories in this region so I don't think it's pointless to have there. Perhaps it could've been abbreviated into one log. Wilson's relentlessly chipper attitude is endearing in small doses, and it works here.

The format itself is great, sharing the same tone as Wilson himself but without being tied directly to the character makes all the lines about their properties very compelling. The combination of outward happiness with implied danger and sinister intent was well done.
